_what: Where Typeless put its paragraph breaks, expressed as the 1-based number of the sentence that STARTS each new paragraph, in the Dictus sentence cut the arms are scored against (PolishSegmentation.sentences, printed in raw/round1-5runs.txt).
_status: REPORTED, NEVER BARRED. bars.md §2: text A is the same four sentences split two different ways on two takes, both defensible, so the reference is one acceptable answer among several. #437 scored against a single correct boundary and that is the mistake this round is built to avoid — in both directions.
_mapping: Typeless rewrites, so its sentences do not map one-to-one onto the Dictus cut. Each break is placed by content: the Dictus sentence whose content opens the Typeless paragraph. Where Typeless deleted a sentence outright (P7 sentence 4, 'Bref, on va avoir un truc qui va être beaucoup plus structuré.'), the break is placed at the next surviving sentence.
_excluded: P2, P4, P5 and P6 have a Typeless output and it is NOT paragraphing: numbered lists, bullets and invented headings, measured in #437 (comment of 2026-08-27 14:39). Its line count there is list structure. Scoring placement against it would fit against a transformation ADR 0003 forbids, so those four carry no reference at all rather than a weak one.

P1-free-form.note: Two paragraphs, the break after 'ce matin en marchant.'. #437 scored this break as over-formatting on a single-idea text and barred it to zero. The maintainer's reading of 2026-09-11 is that it is correct, which is one of the two reasons #550 exists rather than #437 being reopened.

P3-message-draft.note: Three paragraphs: the reason for the absence, the arrangement proposed, and the closing question. 356 characters for 2 breaks is the densest point in the N fit and the one both forms of it miss (bars.md §4).

P7-89s.note: Four paragraphs. These are the same three positions the issue body's pause table names — after '…en plusieurs paragraphes.', '…beaucoup plus structuré.' and '…agréables à lire.' — reached from the text rather than from the audio, which is a consistency check on the alignment that opened the issue and not new evidence for it.
